title: Project configuration manifest contract
description: Objective: freeze the browser-safe, path-neutral V1 data contract that task-5dfc98fc3e7f4035a8012bd9ba032de3 will persist and the benchmark will bind. Deliverable: @moe/contracts public types, closed vocabularies, descriptor-safe parsers, and immutable snapshots for ProjectConfigurationSettings and ProjectConfigurationManifest. The required schema is exact: schemaVersion/projectId; policy revision/evaluator plus MANUAL planning/expansion/acceptance defaults and auto-approval opt-in digest; provider/model/snapshot/reasoning-effort/runtime/profile/structured-output-schema selection refs; a fixed ordered limit table covering design §§2.1, 11.2 and 19.1 (project/goal provider slots, expansion depth/width/nodes/relations, active nodes/hard edges, priority aging/fairness/dispatch bound, review rounds, attempts/runner-authorized time, input sizes/depth, retained events, sessions, capture/tail, subscribers/waiters/outbox/presence, and mandatory artifact quota); provider-egress and daemon-exposure network policy; workspace and host-containment isolation truth; canonical command/query/error schema versions; orchestrationSource as the existing DistributionSource; and settingsDigest only on the full manifest. Logical refs must reject absolute/relative filesystem and file-URI forms. NOT in scope: SHA-256 production, canonical byte encoding, daemon persistence/current selection, benchmark constants, defaults synthesis, or physical configuration paths. Consumer is task-5dfc98fc3e7f4035a8012bd9ba032de3 via the core codec prerequisite created next. Owned paths: packages/contracts/src/configuration/project-configuration-contract.ts, its exact LF .js bridge, focused test, and packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The @moe/contracts root exports the exact V1 settings/manifest types, closed enum and limit-key vocabularies, schema version, and stable refusal code/layer types; the module has no node:* import and remains browser-loadable.

Production parsers use own enumerable data descriptors and exact Reflect.ownKeys snapshots, require dense/fixed-order unique collections and safe bounded values, deep-freeze without aliasing, and pin PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_INPUT_INVALID or PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED at PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_MANIFEST.

The closed contract contains no path key; logical refs reject Windows drive/UNC, POSIX absolute, file URI, dot-segment, accessor, proxy, symbol, extra, missing, duplicate-list, malformed source-sha, and unsupported-version inputs with exact code/layer.

Focused tests import only the bare @moe/contracts root, assert an exact positive schema/hostile-case count, immutable valid snapshots, zero optimistic normalization, and exact failure code/layer for every generated refusal.
The exact verification command exits 0 and task-5dfc98fc3e7f4035a8012bd9ba032de3 is recorded as the production consumer; only the four owned paths are committed explicitly.
taskRails: Do not import node:crypto or any node:* module into the @moe/contracts root; hashing belongs to the dependent core task.
Do not invent or persist defaults: every effective authority value is required input, and missing values fail closed.
Use the existing public DistributionSource shape for orchestration objectFormat/sourceSha; never store a physical repository or configuration path.
The production module must remain <=250 physical lines; split the task before implementation if the exact contract cannot fit without exceeding that target.

The three sections yield roughly 29 keys and the task description's groupings map onto them: 2.1 gives project/goal provider slots, expansion depth/width/nodes, active goal nodes and hard edges, priority-aging quantum, fairness-ticket ceiling, dispatch-decision bound, review rounds; 11.2 gives attempts per node lineage and runner-authorized ms per attempt; 19.1 gives command body bytes, canonical JSON depth, individual string bytes, objective/criterion bytes, submitted expansion relations, active nodes, dispatchable fairness tickets, retained events, active provider sessions, captured output bytes, UI tail bytes, event subscribers, waiters per project, pending outbox rows, presence per second, presence burst, and the mandatory artifact-store byte quota. implementationPlan.description: Implement the parsers in the new packages/contracts/src/configuration/project-configuration-parser.ts plus its LF `.js` bridge. Export `parseProjectConfigurationSettings(value)` and `parseProjectConfigurationManifest(value)`, each returning `{ok:true, settings|manifest} | ProjectConfigurationRefusal`. Build every guard on runtime-guards.js — `isPlainRecord`, `hasExactKeys`, `isSafeArray`, `isHex64`, `isSafeCount`, `isNonEmptyString` — and do NOT reimplement descriptor or proxy handling; the guard order there is already correct and load-bearing. Fixed refusal ORDER, because two guards can both be true and the test pins which one answered: structure first (plain record, exact keys) at INPUT_INVALID, then schemaVersion equality at VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, then field-level validation at INPUT_INVALID. Logical refs: one shared predicate accepting a bounded, well-formed, NFC single token matching a slash-free, backslash-free, colon-free pattern — that one rule categorically excludes drive, drive-relative, UNC, POSIX-absolute, file-URI and dot-segment spellings without enumerating them, which is why the test carries both hostile and legitimate tables. The limit table must be a dense safe array whose length equals PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_LIMIT_KEYS.length, whose entry `i` has `key === PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_LIMIT_KEYS[i]` (fixed order, no sorting and no reordering rescue), each entry an exact two-key own-data record with a safe nonnegative integer value, negative zero refused. Copy every array and record element-by-element into fresh daemon-owned objects and `Object.freeze` the whole result graph without ever freezing or mutating the caller's input. `settingsDigest` is validated on the manifest only, as hex64, and is never synthesized. Nothing here computes a hash, reads a path, or supplies a default. Target <=250 physical lines; if the file crosses it, split the limit-table parsing into a third focused module rather than shrinking comments.
implementationPlan.note:
Parsers landed. project-configuration-parser.ts = 227 lines, bridge 1 line LF. project-configuration-contract.ts grew 213 -> 229 (both under the 250 target), because I refactored isLogicalRef to COMPOSE the existing production isCanonicalText from distribution-contract.js instead of re-spelling isWellFormed/NFC, and added isBoundedText + PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_MAX_TEXT_CHARS. Reusing production rather than duplicating it is the point of the global test rail's "asserted against the production surface, not a helper that reimplements it".

GUARDS ARE ALL BORROWED: isPlainRecord, hasExactKeys, isSafeArray, isHex64, isSafeCount from runtime-guards.js; isCanonicalText and SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS from distribution-contract.js. Zero descriptor/proxy handling written here.

REFUSAL ORDER IS EXPLICIT, not incidental: manifest = isPlainRecord+hasExactKeys (INPUT_INVALID) -> schemaVersion !== literal (VERSION_UNSUPPORTED) -> projectId/settingsDigest/settings (INPUT_INVALID). Settings has no version of its own, so it is structure -> fields only.

LIMIT TABLE is dense and positional: length must equal PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_LIMIT_KEYS.length, `Object.hasOwn(value, index)` rejects a hole left by `delete limits[3]` (a sparse array still reports the right length), entry i must ALREADY carry key i. Nothing sorts, nothing back-fills, nothing is rescued.

TWO PROTOTYPE-POLLUTION DETAILS, deliberate: objectFormat is looked up with `Object.hasOwn(SOURCE_SHA_LENGTHS, objectFormat)` so "__proto__"/"toString" cannot resolve through the chain; closed-vocabulary membership goes through `member()` which type-checks the string first and never coerces a non-string in.

NO NORMALIZATION ANYWHERE: every accepted string is stored as the identical value read from the input; the only substituted literal is schemaVersion, which is provably `===` the input by the equality guard immediately above it. Nothing trims, case-folds, strips "./", or supplies a default. No hash is computed and settingsDigest is validated (hex64) on the manifest only, never synthesized.

IMMUTABILITY: every record and array is rebuilt element-by-element into fresh objects and Object.freeze'd on the way out; the caller's input is never frozen, never mutated, and never aliased into the result.

sourceSha width is taken from the DECLARED objectFormat (sha1 -> 40, sha256 -> 64) and must be lowercase hex, so a valid-looking sha1 presented under sha256 refuses.

D1 ref predicate accepts backslash -> RED "refuses a unc share ref". Precise: the drive rows still refuse via the `:` rule, and all 8 legitimate rows stay green, so the table tests the RULE.

The guard is NOT dead code — it is the only defense against a polluted Array.prototype filling the hole with a valid-looking entry, and no test could reach it. D6 drop the `!optIn && digest !== null` leg -> RED "refuses fully manual gates carrying an opt-in digest", proving the cross-rule is bidirectional.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: SCOPE DECISION THAT NEEDS TO BE READ FIRST. The task description names four owned paths and task rail 4 says to split the TASK if the exact contract cannot fit in one <=250-line module. It cannot: the schema alone is a ~29-key ordered limit vocabulary, five closed enums, seven selection refs, network, isolation, three schema versions, orchestrationSource, two interfaces and a refusal vocabulary, and the descriptor-safe parsers for all of it. The project's global size rule, which is newer and binds architects explicitly, resolves this the other way: 'do not SPIDR-split a task because its total diff is projected over 400 lines... a large task made of small focused files is fully compliant... split when a single production FILE would exceed 400 lines, or when responsibilities are genuinely separable.' Vocabulary versus parsing IS genuinely separable and is already how this package is organised (distribution-contract.ts 164 lines + distribution-parser.ts 248 lines + distribution-verifier.ts 235 lines; document-work-proposal-contract.ts + -codec.ts). planningNotes.risks:
1. INVENTED DEFAULTS ARE THE MOST LIKELY REJECTION. The design prints the numbers (4, 3, 6, 9, 24, 64, 10000, 1 MiB, ...) and it is tempting to freeze them beside the keys. Task rail 2 forbids it: the contract fixes the key vocabulary and order only, and every value is required caller input that fails closed when absent.
2. AN OVER-NARROWED REF MATCHER PASSES EVERY HOSTILE ROW. A predicate that refuses everything satisfies the whole drive/UNC/file-URI table. The legitimate-ref positive-control table is not optional; without it the hostile table proves nothing.
3. GUARD ORDER IS ASSERTABLE AND MUST BE PINNED. A record that is BOTH structurally hostile and version-unsupported can be answered by either code. Fix the order — structure, then version, then fields — and drill it (D4), or the code the test asserts is an accident of implementation.
4. `export type` IS ERASED AT RUNTIME. A type-only publication typechecks while nothing is importable. The root test must reach a real runtime value from each new module.
5. BROWSER SAFETY IS TRANSITIVE. Asserting the two new sources are free of `node:` is necessary but the imports they pull in matter too; runtime-guards.ts is safe by design (documented runtime lookup) and distribution-contract.ts is type-only for DistributionSource. Do not add any other import without checking it.
6. THE `.js` BRIDGE IS LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO BOTCH. Intra-package imports use `.js` specifiers, so a missing bridge breaks runtime loading while tsc stays green; and a CRLF bridge on Windows would differ from every sibling. Verify with `git ls-files --eol` after adding.
7. SHARED WORKTREE. Other agents hold uncommitted work under .moe/**, packages/runner/**, packages/store/** and apps/daemon/**. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; `git add` the five new files explicitly before committing by six-path pathspec.
8. A GENERATED SWEEP THAT PRODUCES NOTHING PASSES. Every hostile matrix and every vocabulary list must be checked against a HAND-WRITTEN count or list, never against one derived from the exports under test.
